answer.rationale: The hard constraint is not increasing delivery risk with the line at 94% and no buffer and a primary contract that ends in 14 days without auto-renewal. Deferral or adding a second source as the sole action would leave a coverage gap. Incumbent already refused to reopen price this cycle, so negotiate_terms is unlikely to land an 18% cut inside the window and could spend the only decision. memory_c1 supports renewal as the path that keeps integration and deliveries intact. memory_c2 suggests a low-cost switch can cut unit cost with fast onboarding, which is the only plausible way to hit the spend cut, but “quick last year” is not evidenced to be compatible with a 14-day cutover at this utilization; verifying that record before treating switch as safe. Until then, renew the incumbent on current terms; TCO cut and single-source exposure remain unresolved for the next cycle.
